answers.answer: Each player uses the chosen hero’s matching components; shuffle that hero’s 30 action cards into a separate face-down deck and draw 5. Set dials to the listed starting health (undialed sidekicks have 1). Younger player places hero on space 1, then sidekicks in separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero; for a multizone hero space, use any of its zones. Older player then places hero on space 2 and sidekicks the same way. Alice’s controller chooses BIG or SMALL when placing her. Younger player takes the first turn.

evidence.text:
1. Choose a battlefield and place it on the table. Each player chooses a hero and takes that hero’s components.
2. Set the hero’s and sidekick’s dials to the starting health above; undialed sidekicks have 1 health each.
3. Each player shuffles their **30 action cards into one separate face-down deck**, then draws **5 cards**.
4. The **younger player** places their hero on starting space **1**, then their sidekick(s) in **separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero**. If the hero’s space belongs to several zones, use any of those zones. Make beginning-of-game decisions when placing that player’s fighters. **Alice’s controller**, whether younger or older, chooses **BIG or SMALL when placing Alice** and displays her size token.
5. The **older player** places their hero on starting space **2**, then places sidekicks under the same rules.
6. The younger player takes the first turn.

clauses: Number and types of required turn actions.

answers.answer: Take 2 actions from maneuver, scheme, and attack; actions may be repeated, but neither action may be skipped. Holding 9 during the turn is allowed; at turn end discard 2 cards to your own discard pile, leaving 7, before the opponent’s turn.

evidence.text: At the start of Medusa’s turn, her optional special ability may resolve (see below). Then take **2 actions** from **maneuver, scheme, attack**. You may repeat an action, including maneuver twice; **you cannot skip an action**.
You may hold more than 7 cards during your turn. **At the end of your turn**, discard excess cards to your own discard pile until you have **7**, then the opponent takes their turn.

clauses: Order of drawing and movement during an ordinary maneuver.
Which fighters move, each fighter’s distance allowance, and whether movement may be zero.
Passage through friendly versus opposing fighters, ending on occupied spaces, and whether fighters’ movement may be interleaved.
answers.answer: Draw 1 card first, mandatorily. Then you may move each fighter independently up to its move value, including zero; finish one fighter’s movement before starting another. You may pass through friendly fighters, but may not pass through opposing fighters or finish on any occupied space. Thus the moves cannot be interleaved.

evidence.text:
1. **Draw 1 card first, mandatory.**
2. **Optionally move** each of your fighters, one at a time, up to your move value (plus applicable bonuses). Each fighter chooses its own distance, including **zero**. Choose their order, but finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s.

Ordinary movement enters adjacent spaces along connecting lines. You may pass through your own friendly fighters, but **cannot finish in any occupied space**. You may **not pass through opposing fighters**. An effect that moves opposing fighters follows the same rules **from their owner’s perspective**. Apply these movement restrictions to card movement unless that card states an exception.

answers.answer: During a maneuver, discard one hand card and add its printed BOOST value (not combat value) to that maneuver’s movement value. Ignore the discarded card’s effects. Every one of your fighters gets the increased allowance, and even a card unusable because its fighter is defeated may pay for BOOST.

Each of your fighters receives that allowance. Ignore the discarded card’s effects. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated **can still be discarded to BOOST**. Effects may separately permit boosting attacks; boosting is not otherwise a universal option.

clauses: Whether the two mandatory draws are declined or trigger exhaustion, and whether the discard pile is reshuffled.

answers.answer: The draws cannot be declined and the discard pile is not reshuffled. With an empty deck, each missing draw deals 2 damage to every fighter; across two missing draws, each surviving fighter takes 4 damage total, as two separate 2-damage events.

evidence.text: - Drawing cards, whether from maneuver or an effect, is **mandatory unless explicitly optional**.

- With an empty deck, your fighters are **exhausted**. Each time you must draw a card you cannot draw, **each of your fighters immediately takes 2 damage instead**. Do **not reshuffle** your discard pile. A mandatory draw of 2 with an empty deck therefore causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter, unless hero defeat has already ended the game. If only one card remains, draw it and take the exhaustion damage for the next missing draw.

answers.answer: An attack action is illegal without an attack-capable card in hand or a valid target. Declare the attacking fighter and opposing target first. Then the attacker commits an allowed attack card face down; the defender may decline or commit a legal defense card face down. Reveal simultaneously after both choices. evidence.text: 1. **Declare** your attacking fighter (active fighter) and the opposing fighter targeted. 2. **Choose cards:** attacker plays an attack card face down that the attacking fighter is allowed to use. Defender may decline to play a card; otherwise plays a legal defense card face down for the defending fighter. **Reveal simultaneously** after both choices.

Attack-only cards are red, defense-only blue, and **versatile** cards purple. Versatile cards may attack or defend and **count as both attack and defense cards for other effects**. A fighter-specific card cannot be used by a different fighter; **ANY** permits any of your fighters. A pure defense card cannot initiate an attack; a pure attack card cannot defend.

clauses: Full order of card-effect timing, damage resolution, other after-combat effects, and discard.

answers.answer: Resolve immediately effects, then during-combat effects, determine and apply combat damage, resolve after-combat card effects, resolve other after-combat game effects, then put all played cards in their owners’ discard piles. For effects sharing a timing, defender resolves first. Effects are mandatory unless they say otherwise.

evidence.text:
1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective discard piles.

**Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first.** Card effects are **mandatory unless they say otherwise** (for example “may”); this can harm your own fighters. Complete them in the printed order. A card whose effects are canceled keeps its printed combat value; the canceled effects do not resolve.
